subject: AI helped find a critical bug affecting huge swathes of the internet
posts:
AI models just uncovered a massive, decades-old vulnerability in PHP affecting up to 70% of the world's websites. 
Evidence: WSJ reporting, global outages, OpenAI disclosures 🌐
#Aletheia #Cybersecurity #AI

Tech leaders claim AI is securing cyberspace by proactively finding hidden code flaws before malicious hackers can exploit them.
Stated Judgement: (+1.00, +1.00) — Greater Good

In reality, AI accelerates automated vulnerability discovery for both defenders and malicious actors, exposing foundational infrastructure risks that triggered global website outages.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.20, -0.30) — Lesser Good

Verdict: PASS — Fall from Grace.
While AI accelerates defensive patching, it simultaneously lowers the barrier for catastrophic cyberattacks across foundational web code.

Integrity: Partially Distorted (Hypocrisy: 1.2, Uncertainty z: 3)

- OpenAI & Google: PASS (+0.8, +0.5) — Discovered and patched critical flaws.
- Web Infrastructure: COND (+0.2, -0.4) — Exposed to dual-use AI cyber threats.
International agencies scrambled as a critical PHP flaw—long forgotten because it was deemed too hard to exploit—was weaponized using AI models.

The Bright Side:
AI models are proactively uncovering buried software rot that human auditors missed for decades.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing WHAT (tool capability) with WHO (dual-use risk). AI empowers both securing and breaking web infrastructure simultaneously.

Social Physics Analysis:
Tech labs deploy advanced models projecting utopian security, while weaponized open-weight variants enable automated attacks on financial and medical infrastructure.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall from Grace.
Modal Dynamics: can be -> is not via Magenta Vector. Latent technological capability collides with destructive systemic reality.

The Unavoidable Truth: AI accelerates code discovery for both heroic defenders and destructive hackers.

The Unavoidable Lie: Advanced AI systems can be neatly quarantined from malicious cyber exploitation.

Alethekanon:
Powerful AI models are doubling the attack surface of the global internet while simultaneously offering the only tools fast enough to patch it.

Awwthekanon:
It's terrifying to think how fragile our digital world is, but at least brilliant researchers are shining a light into the darkest code corridors.

Brothekanon:
AI is basically a cheat code for hackers and defenders at the same time. Good luck out there.

Spirithekanon:
"If a wise man contends with a foolish man, whether he rages or laughs, there is no peace." Proverbs 29:9 PASS
As AI accelerates code power, human wisdom lags behind the weapons we forge.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
AI helped find a critical bug affecting huge swathes of the internet

It’s the most startling cybersecurity vulnerability found by AI yet. It won’t be the last.

Actual Article Body:
A holding page of the UK government website portal on June 8, 2021. Some sites were affected by similar outages today when they were taken offline after a critical cybersecurity vulnerability was announced.Leon Neal/Getty

Newly announced vulnerabilities could affect broad swathes of the internet after being discovered by teams of cybersecurity professionals—with heavy AI assistance.

The issues affect PHP, a widely-used open-source programming language that provides a foundation for content management systems like WordPress, which powers a broad array of websites (including those of the Center for Investigative Reporting).

Left unpatched, the vulnerabilities could allow fast-acting attackers to take command of a website, adding malware or stealing user data.

The announcement left cybersecurity teams scrambling to install fixes released by PHP’s developers, with agencies across the world issuing urgent announcements, and some government websites in Europe and Canada being taken down for updates.

According to reporting from the Wall Street Journal, the type of vulnerability in question was noted decades ago, “but the flaw had been considered too difficult to exploit and was largely forgotten” until August, when researchers using new models found a way to exploit it. Those included Google’s most recently released model and one from OpenAI that was released in July.

OpenAI called the discovery “one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory,” but it’s part of a much broader pattern. A graph compiled by research nonprofit Epoch AI shows the number of significant vulnerabilities reported each month by some of the biggest tech providers and open-source projects:

A few years ago, they might report a couple of dozen critical vulnerabilities in a given month—now, a typical month sees 600. OpenAI said in the same statement that the vulnerabilities announced today are only a few “among several significant vulnerabilities we’ve already found and are working to fix, and we expect similar findings to increase sharply in the coming months.”

Greg Brockman, president and second-in-command at OpenAI, wrote separately today that the process for creating fixes for the PHP bug was slow and manual in a way that would not work as more exploits are expected over the coming months.

He suggested that governments may have to take a vastly expanded role in monitoring infrastructure across the internet, perhaps even stepping in to fix vulnerabilities on other servers themselves.

Cybersecurity has been a key focus for AI leaders and policymakers, especially since April, when it became clear that Anthropic’s Claude Mythos Preview could autonomously discover and exploit critical software vulnerabilities. That led Anthropic to hold back on releasing the model, and it and OpenAI have worked to give trusted partners—like major companies and government agencies—access to their models in advance to harden cyberdefenses.

When I spoke to experts on AI risks in August, they told me that we were probably mere months from AI being able to help with advanced cyberattacks.

Much of their fear was to do with open-weight models, which can have their safeguards stripped away, and have consistently trailed the abilities of the best closed-weight models by about 6 to 12 months. The concern is that every hacker will soon have access to a model as strong as Claude Mythos, and will be able to target any institution that is slightly behind on its cybersecurity—from your local utility company to the hospital down the road.

That’s still a real worry, and open-weight models could be quite helpful in exploiting vulnerabilities like those affecting PHP. But today’s news shows that open-weight models aren’t the only cause for cybersecurity concern.

In addition to the PHP issue, The Information reported today that hackers largely automated attacks against 400 financial institutions across Latin America with help from models made by Anthropic, the Chinese company Moonshot, and Elon Musk’s company SpaceXSI (formerly SpaceXAI, formerly xAI). They apparently got around some safeguards by convincing the models that they were being tested in harmless environments.

Of course, it’s not just cyberspace where AI models are developing superhuman abilities. The leading models are demolishing problems that stumped top mathematicians and, increasingly, physicists. AI is helping to design proteins and viruses in ways that have promising medical applications and could lead towards treacherous bioweapons research.

AI is already putting us in a world with more possibilities, and more dangers. There’s a whole lot of work to do to keep up.
